cards.title: GKSL generator in the paper's vectorization convention
cards.latex: \operatorname{vec}(|i\rangle\langle j|)=|i\rangle|j\rangle,\qquad \mathbf L=-i(H\otimes I-I\otimes H^T)+\sum_k\left[L_k\otimes\overline{L_k}-\frac12 L_k^\dagger L_k\otimes I-\frac12I\otimes(L_k^\dagger L_k)^T\right],\qquad \operatorname{vec}[\rho(t)]=e^{t\mathbf L}\operatorname{vec}[\rho(0)]
cards.role: Fixes the basis ordering, transpose convention, and matrix exponential used independently for both numerical figures.

checks.reason: The vectorization identity and Liouville-space construction are printed in Supplemental Sec. A; applying that identity independently fixes the transpose placement shown here.
Contracting the generator with vec(I) gives zero: each jump contribution has one gain term and two equal half-loss terms, while the commutator is traceless.
For H=0 and L=sqrt(Gamma)|0><1|, exponentiation gives rho_11(t)=exp(-Gamma t)rho_11(0) and rho_01(t)=exp(-Gamma t/2)rho_01(0), the standard amplitude-damping channel.

cards.numerical_form: Build the d^2-by-d^2 complex matrix with NumPy Kronecker products and evaluate scipy.linalg.expm(t*L).
open_questions: The supplemental displayed generator places the two loss-term transposes inconsistently with vec(ABC)=(A tensor C^T)vec(B). The independently derived formula above is used; both paper numerics have real diagonal L^dagger L, so the typo does not affect the reproduced targets.

cards.title: Liouville-to-Choi reshuffling
cards.latex: J(\mathcal E_t)=\sum_{i,j=0}^{d-1}|i\rangle\langle j|\otimes\mathcal E_t(|i\rangle\langle j|)=\sum_{i,j,a,b=0}^{d-1}K_{ab,ij}(t)|i\rangle\langle j|\otimes|a\rangle\langle b|,\qquad K(t)=e^{t\mathbf L}
cards.role: Converts each generated Lindblad channel into the unnormalized Choi matrix used as both target channel and program resource.

checks.reason: The index-level reshuffling is printed in Supplemental Sec. A.
For K=I_(d^2), the formula gives |I>><<I|, whose trace is d and whose output partial trace is I_d.
Therefore pi_t=J(E_t)/d has unit trace, exactly matching the author scripts' division by d.

cards.numerical_form: Reshape K[out_row,out_col,in_row,in_col] and transpose to J[in_row,out_row,in_col,out_col], then flatten.

cards.title: Exact factorization of the SWAP-dephasing semigroup
cards.latex: \mathcal L=i\,\operatorname{ad}_S+\lambda(\mathcal D_{\mathbb B}-\mathcal I),\qquad e^{t\mathcal L}=e^{-\lambda t}e^{it\operatorname{ad}_S}+(1-e^{-\lambda t})\mathcal D_{\mathbb B},\qquad e^{it\operatorname{ad}_S}(\rho)=e^{itS}\rho e^{-itS}
cards.role: Separates Fig. 2 into an exactly programmable coherent branch and a physical Bell-dephasing branch.

checks.reason: The generator and factorized channel are stated in the main text and proved in the Supplemental Material.
S is diagonal in the Bell basis, so ad_S commutes with Bell dephasing and the two exponentials factor.
D_B^2=D_B implies exp[lambda t(D_B-I)]=exp(-lambda t)I+[1-exp(-lambda t)]D_B; D_B after the SWAP unitary is still D_B.
At t=0 the channel is identity; at long times it approaches Bell-basis dephasing.

cards.numerical_form: Use the analytic convex mixture for the reference curve and construct the full 16-by-16 Liouvillian independently as a cross-check.

cards.title: Fixed two-level HPTP processor for the coherent SWAP branch
cards.role: Provides an independent, fixed HPTP map for the nonphysical branch sampled in Fig. 2, without importing the authors' stored Choi matrices.

checks.reason: The map M, the two projectors, and the program state are given in the Supplemental proof.
M is Hermiticity preserving; the diagonal program blocks contribute one half of the trace each and the off-diagonal blocks are traceless under orthogonal projectors, so P is HPTP.
Substitution of the normalized program state yields sum_ab exp[i(s_a-s_b)t] Pi_a rho Pi_b=e^{itS}rho e^{-itS}.

cards.numerical_form: Construct P from its action on the 8-by-8 matrix-unit basis, then build its 32-by-32 unnormalized Choi matrix.

cards.title: Signed CPTP decomposition and unbiased quasi-sampling
cards.latex: \mathcal P=p_+\mathcal E_+-p_-\mathcal E_-,\qquad p_+-p_-=1,\qquad \kappa=p_++p_-=\|\mathcal P\|_\diamond,\qquad q_\pm=\frac{p_\pm}{\kappa},\qquad \widehat o=\kappa\,s_\alpha o_\alpha,\quad \mathbb E[\widehat o]=\operatorname{tr}[O\mathcal P(\rho)]
cards.role: Turns the HPTP processor into physical channel samples and makes the estimator, normalization, and sampling overhead explicit.

checks.reason: The signed-channel decomposition and its operational sampling interpretation are stated in the main text and Supplemental preliminaries.
Trace preservation of P and both E branches forces p_+-p_-=1.
Summing q_alpha*kappa*s_alpha*tr[O E_alpha(rho)] gives p_+o_+-p_-o_-, exactly the HPTP expectation.

cards.numerical_form: Solve the small Choi SDP for p_plus, p_minus, J_plus, J_minus; sample branches with probabilities p/kappa using a fixed recorded seed.

cards.title: Programming cost versus plotted sampling overhead
cards.latex: \gamma_\epsilon(\pi_t,\mathcal L,T)=\log_2\min_{\mathcal P\in\Omega}\left\{\|\mathcal P\|_\diamond:\ \frac12\|\mathcal P(\cdot\otimes\pi_t)-e^{t\mathcal L}\|_\diamond\le\epsilon\ \forall t\in[0,T]\right\},\qquad \kappa_\epsilon:=2^{\gamma_\epsilon}=\min\|\mathcal P\|_\diamond
cards.role: Separates the logarithmic resource monotone from the linear sampling overhead actually shown on Fig. 3's vertical axis.

checks.reason: The main text explicitly specifies a binary logarithm; the source figure labels its ordinate 2^{gamma_epsilon(L)}.
The disclosed MATLAB scripts store cost_array=p1+p2 without applying a logarithm, confirming that the plotted quantity is kappa_epsilon.
A physical retrieval channel has diamond norm one, hence kappa=1 and gamma=0 as required by faithfulness.

cards.numerical_form: Optimize kappa=p_plus+p_minus directly; report both kappa and log2(kappa), but plot kappa to match Fig. 3.

The three partial-trace constraints imply p_+-p_-=1, while the objective is the signed-channel one-norm p_++p_-.

checks.reason: The contraction appears in Supplemental Eq. B1 and is implemented with the same subsystem order in the disclosed scripts.
Expanding J^P in program matrix units contracts pi_ba, which is exactly multiplication by pi^T followed by tracing P.
If Tr_S' J^P=I_SP and Tr pi=1, then Tr_S' J[P_pi]=I_S, so the retrieved map is trace preserving.

cards.title: Diamond norm SDP for Hermiticity-preserving maps

source_refs.value: Watrous, Semidefinite Programs for Completely Bounded Norms (2009)
Watrous, Simpler semidefinite programs for completely bounded norms (2012)

cards.role: Replaces the authors' QETLAB call by a transparent small SDP and fixes the factor of two in the epsilon constraint.

checks.reason: The general block SDP is given by Watrous and used by QETLAB; for Hermitian Choi matrices its two positive variables can be symmetrized to one Z.
For Hermitian J, averaging the two Watrous variables gives equal blocks Z; a block Hadamard transform converts positivity of [[Z,-J],[-J,Z]] into Z+J>=0 and Z-J>=0.
For the identity channel, choosing Z=J(identity) gives Tr_out Z=I and diamond norm one.

cards.numerical_form: For each channel difference use a Hermitian Z with Z±J_delta positive semidefinite; half-diamond<=epsilon sets Tr_out(Z)<=2*epsilon*I.

cards.title: Fig. 3 Lindbladians, Choi programs, and disclosed finite grids
cards.role: Pins every physical and discretization parameter needed to reproduce the blue and red Fig. 3 curves.

checks.reason: The figure fixes epsilon and T; the public scripts fix Gamma=0.1, H=0 or Z, n=1, sample=1000, and the 41-point epsilon grid.
MATLAB forms 0:T/sample:T but loops j=1:sample, so the optimized grid contains 1000 points from 0 through 9.99 and omits the allocated endpoint 10.
Each program resource is J(A_t)/2 and has trace one; the target passed to DiamondNorm is 2*pi_t=J(A_t).

cards.numerical_form: Generate both branches from the Liouvillian, solve the author-exact 1000-point grid, and separately test inclusion of t=10 as a discretization sensitivity check.
open_questions: The caption describes [0,10], while the disclosed numerical loop enforces 0<=t<=9.99. The final evidence must report the author-exact curve and a separate endpoint-inclusion sensitivity result.

cards.title: HPTP implementability cost and composition behavior

source_refs.value: Supplement physical implementability section, fresh items R048-R056

cards.latex: \nu(\mathcal N)=\log_2\min\{\eta_++\eta_-:\mathcal N=\eta_+\mathcal E_+-\eta_-\mathcal E_-,\ \mathcal E_\pm\ \mathrm{CPTP}\},\qquad \nu(\mathcal N)=\log_2\|\mathcal N\|_\diamond\ \text{for TP maps}
cards.role: Owns the signed-channel implementability resource and preserves a finite counterexample to the supplement's printed composition equality.

checks.reason: The supplement states the signed two-channel cost, tensor and composition behavior, unitary invariance, mitigation overhead, and TP diamond-norm relation in one physical-implementability section.
A non-CP trace-preserving Pauli map is reconstructed from exactly two CPTP channels; its Choi trace norm divided by d equals the signed one-norm.
The witness obeys tensor additivity and unitary pre/post invariance, and an invertible bit-flip noise channel is explicitly inverted.
Composing the signed map with a 50/50 bit-flip CPTP channel strictly reduces overhead from the product bound 2 to 1, contradicting a universal equality while satisfying subadditivity.

cards.numerical_form: Use orthogonal Pauli-channel Choi sectors to evaluate signed one-norm costs, tensor products, compositions, unitary conjugations, and a noise inverse without author arrays or source pixels.
open_questions: Fresh review must decide whether the supplement intended a composition inequality instead of the printed equality; author-side evidence records the counterexample but cannot promote a paper-error verdict.
